source.title: Pitfalls of Scale: Investigating the Inverse Task of Redefinition in Large Language Models
source.authors: Elena Stringli; Maria Lymperaiou; Giorgos Filandrianos; Athanasios Voulodimos; G. Stamou

record.tranche_reason: Tests how model scale relates to performance on a newly designed redefinition reasoning task, a different measure and setting from the loss-scaling claims.
record.gate_note: The paper measures redefinition-task response accuracy and anchoring across models, including comparisons by model size. It does not measure held-out cross-entropy loss, fit loss power laws, or test compute-optimal parameter/token allocations.
record.test_reason: Compares Llama 3.1 8B/70B/405B and Mistral 7B/Mixtral 8x7B/Mistral Large on a downstream redefinition task. It finds anchoring errors rise with size and frames this as inverse scaling against predictable gains, so it bears on V6. It measures no loss, fits no power laws and varies no allocation or shape, so V1–V5 and V7 are not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that larger models anchor more to memorized values on redefinition tasks (inverse scaling), and that prompting and format change but do not eliminate anchoring. Add that they also report larger models refuse less, which they call rising false confidence. Note also that their text admits larger models reach higher post-redefinition correct rates even as anchoring rises.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates accuracy and anchoring on redefinition prompts across deployed language models; it does not measure the original studies’ held-out loss scaling recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: Anchoring varies with redefinition type, question difficulty, prompt method, and response format. The paper reports that MC generally has more anchoring than FF; few-shot prompting often reduces anchoring, while CoT does not reliably do so. Unit-redefinition patterns differ from constant-redefinition patterns.

fits_no_version.finding: Refusal to perform the redefinition falls with model size (e.g. Llama8B ZS FF 55.54% vs Llama405B 0%, Table 9). The authors read this as false confidence growing with scale.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Larger LLMs abstain less when given a counterfactual premise, scale-dependent refusal behaviour.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 19 models, no-redefinition accuracy correlates positively with anchoring on Q3 swaps (r≈0.67–0.75, Table 7). The correlation is negative on Q1/Q2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: More capable models anchor more to memorized priors on hard counterfactual reasoning, a capability-based (not size-based) inverse trend.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics, 2025
record.problems: The study evaluates a restricted, manually designed redefinition task rather than pretraining loss or a broad set of downstream benchmarks. It compares different model families and sizes rather than controlled size variants throughout; the authors note the closed-world task scope and do not conduct a human comparison. Table 8 results have no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: None of the selected Table 8 results were left out; additional models, question levels, prompt methods, response formats, unit-redefinition results, and results shown only in figures were not extracted because the record is limited to 18 rows.

untested.parts: Held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
Extrapolation of small-run fits to larger runs.
Shape or architecture at fixed parameter count.
Predictability from pretraining loss (no losses are reported). No fitted trend: only 3 sizes per family, n=15–16 questions per cell, no uncertainty. No broad benchmark suite.
Dependence of fitted exponents or allocations on setup or fitting choices.

missing.what: MC-format Q3 Rs2 anchoring by size: Llama 20.0/73.33/93.33; Mistral 20.0/73.33/66.67. This is the strongest inverse-scaling evidence.
Anchoring by size under FS and CoT prompting on Ra3/Rs2 Q3, MC format
Post-redefinition correct-response rates by size. The text says larger models get higher correct rates, which conflicts with the abstract's 'performance degrades with scale'.
Units-of-measure redefinition anchoring by size (e.g. Ra3 Q3 FF Llama 25.0/12.5/25.0, Mistral 31.25/31.25/12.5). These are mixed despite the text claiming a consistent inverse trend.

record.verdict_notes: Evidence is thin for a scaling claim: 3 sizes per family, and Mistral sizes span different architectures and releases. Cells are 15 questions (one item = 6.67 points) with no uncertainty. The answer judge is Claude 3.5 Sonnet. The record's 'partial' states on the anchoring rows were wrong: rising anchoring with size is reversed relative to V6. Not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss as a function of parameters, tokens, or compute.
Whether power-law fits from small runs predict larger-run loss.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocations and their trends with compute.

Power-law behavior in other modalities or training regimes.

relationships.condition: Q3 constant redefinitions, hardest levels (Ra3, Rs2), ZS, FF; largest Llama (405B) and Mistral (Large 123B) models
relationships.reason: Anchoring errors rise with size: Llama Rs2 26.67→33.33→53.33 and Mistral Rs2 26.67→46.67→73.33 (R11, R12, R17, R18). Largest models also anchor more on Ra3 (R9, R15). The paper states the inverse trend explicitly.
relationships.display_finding: Rs2 anchoring errors rose from 26.67 to 33.33 to 53.33 for Llama and 26.67 to 46.67 to 73.33 for Mistral, while the largest models also anchored more on Ra3.

relationships.condition: Same task; intermediate sizes and no-redefinition performance
relationships.reason: The trend is non-monotone. Llama 70B Ra3 anchoring equals 8B (R8) and Mixtral Ra3 anchors less than 7B (R14). No-redefinition accuracy peaks at the middle size in both families (R1–R6).
relationships.display_finding: Llama 70B matched 8B on Ra3 anchoring, Mixtral anchored less than 7B, and no-redefinition accuracy peaked at intermediate sizes in both families.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Q3 constant-redefinition task, ZS prompting, FF response format; Llama family, especially Rs 2
reader_labels.reason: Anchoring, which the study classifies as an incorrect redefined-task response, rises from 8B to 405B in both listed redefinition conditions (R7–R12). The paper also explicitly reports that anchoring increases with scale on this task.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Q3 constant-redefinition task, ZS prompting, FF response format; Mistral family
reader_labels.reason: The size trend depends on the redefinition: rates rise from 7B to 123B for Rs 2 but are not monotonic for Ra 3; no-redefinition correct rates also do not increase monotonically across the three Llama sizes (R1–R6, R13–R18).
